system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The alert is marked Actual with Extreme severity, but it names no hazard, time or place. The only event input has empty text, so there is no hazard bulletin behind it. The description 'misantropi4' looks like test or erroneous content. Nothing in this alert can be checked against hazard facts, and it should not go out as an Actual Extreme alert. A person must decide whether this is a false or test alert and whether to stop it.

objections.issue: The alert names no hazard event. The event and headline say only 'Alerta Extremo', and the description is a meaningless string rather than a description of a hazard. The only input has null text, so there is no bulletin to support any hazard. The content looks like a test or erroneous message sent as Actual.
objections.fix: Hold the alert. A person must confirm with the issuing authority whether a real hazard exists. If one does, redraft the event, headline and description from the verified bulletin, giving the hazard, times and areas. If not, cancel the alert and treat it as a false alert.

objections.issue: Severity Extreme and urgency Immediate claim an extraordinary threat to life or property, but no verified input supports this. Certainty is Unknown, so the alert asserts maximum severity while admitting it does not know whether the event exists. Severity is set higher than any bulletin supports.
objections.fix: Set severity, urgency and certainty only from a verified hazard bulletin. With no bulletin, Extreme/Immediate cannot be supported and the alert should not be issued.
